metadata.title: Why a 99%-Accurate Test Is Almost Always Wrong When It Says Yes
metadata.purpose: Show how a rare base rate drowns a high-accuracy test in false positives, making a positive result almost uninformative. Source: books/computational-skepticism-for-ai/chapters/02-probability-uncertainty-and-the-confidence-illusion.md
metadata.color_semantics: TEAL = true positives / correctly flagged; CRIMSON = false positives / noise in the bucket; GOLD = the base rate / the key number; SLATE = healthy population
metadata.note: EXCLUSIONS: no Bayes' theorem formula or derivation, no sensitivity/specificity vocabulary, no odds-form shortcut, no second domain example
